title: Transaction Monitoring Review
summary: Reconcile a transaction extract, calculate transparent monitoring scenarios, and turn rule matches into reviewable observations with explicit benign explanations.
audience: Monitoring analysts, scenario owners, and independent control reviewers
decision: Which scenario matches merit further review, which have supported explanations, and which cannot be assessed because the inputs are incomplete?
report_sections: Limitations, quality checks, and human decision

raw_row_id.description: Immutable identifier of one delivered source row. Repeated economic transactions retain distinct raw-row identifiers so extraction duplicates remain countable.

transaction_id.description: Source economic transaction identifier. Its uniqueness is assessed with account leg and source version; matching amount or narrative alone is insufficient.

account_id.description: Fictional account key at the declared grain. Account and customer are different units; no aggregation across accounts occurs without an explicit bridge.

event_utc.description: Timezone-aware economic event instant serialized in UTC. The source-local representation belongs in evidence; elapsed comparisons use this instant.

direction.description: Canonical CREDIT or DEBIT from the account perspective. Amount remains nonnegative; do not infer direction from a signed display string.

amount_text.description: Exact source amount string before parsing. It can contain unreadable text; preserve it as evidence and never sum it directly.

currency.description: Explicit row currency. USD and EUR remain separate; the specimen contains no foreign-exchange conversion or implicit base-currency amount.

counterparty_id.description: Supplied counterparty reference for this economic leg. Similar names or repeated identifiers do not independently establish common ownership.

posting_state.description: Canonical posting status that determines whether a leg enters the declared posted population. A pending item remains visible outside that population.

ownership_state.description: Evidence-backed own/external classification for the specific leg and historical period. Unknown ownership is not automatically external or own.

terminal_bucket.description: Exactly one initial raw-row reconciliation outcome. It explains whether the row is processed, duplicate or unreadable; scenario exclusions are a separate layer.

evidence_ids.description: Semicolon-delimited exact Evidence keys. Every key must resolve, support the row proposition and retain its claim class and scope limitation.

domain_tables.name: AccountFlows

account_id.description: Fictional account key at the declared grain. Account and customer are different units; no aggregation across accounts occurs without an explicit bridge.

currency.description: Explicit row currency. USD and EUR remain separate; the specimen contains no foreign-exchange conversion or implicit base-currency amount.

processed_tx_count.description: Count of readable canonical economic legs at account/currency grain. It excludes extraction duplicates and unknown-amount rows but retains own transfers.

credit_total.description: Known eligible or gross credit subtotal as specified by the table grain. It is not necessarily a complete total when coverage_state or population_status is defective.

debit_total.description: Known eligible debit subtotal at the table grain. Null is required for a window total dependent on an unknown debit; known subtotals elsewhere remain explicitly partial.

eligible_credit_total.description: Sum of known credit amounts after stated scenario exclusions. It cannot include confirmed own legs or a copied extraction duplicate.

eligible_debit_total.description: Sum of known debit amounts after stated scenario exclusions. It is not an attributed or suspicious amount and may exceed eligible credits.

out_in_ratio.description: Eligible debit total divided by positive eligible credit total. Stored as a dimensionless ratio and displayed as a percentage without changing decision precision.

population_status.description: Account-level completeness or exclusion state. COMPLETE, OWN_TRANSFER_EXCLUDED and UNPARSED_AMOUNT have different analytical consequences.

domain_tables.name: WindowDiagnostics
domain_tables.title: Observed credit-anchored membership; coverage remains incomplete

window_id.description: Stable account/anchor/specification window key. It distinguishes overlapping observations so a membership count cannot be mistaken for unique transactions.

account_id.description: Fictional account key at the declared grain. Account and customer are different units; no aggregation across accounts occurs without an explicit bridge.

anchor_leg_id.description: Canonical eligible credit that starts a diagnostic window. Only credit anchors are used; a debit cannot silently become an anchor.

start_utc.description: Inclusive UTC instant at the anchor. The applicable window convention determines endpoint inclusion, not the date formatting of the rendered table.

end_utc.description: UTC endpoint exactly 24 elapsed hours after the anchor. The scenario-design closed interval includes this instant; the TM diagnostic convention matches it.

observed_leg_ids.description: Semicolon-delimited canonical legs observed inside the diagnostic interval. This list is partial when the extract does not cover the entire interval.

known_credit_total.description: Sum of readable credits only at the declared stage, account or observed diagnostic window. The word known is substantive where an unresolved amount exists.

known_debit_total.description: Sum of readable debits only at the declared stage, account or observed diagnostic window. An unknown debit is not imputed as a measured zero.

known_ratio.description: Ratio of known observed debits to known observed credits when the denominator is positive. Boundary-incomplete diagnostics do not establish a complete rule result.

first_debit_hours.description: Elapsed hours from anchor to first strictly subsequent eligible debit. Null means no qualifying ordered pair; a contemporaneous debit cannot satisfy the predicate.

coverage_state.description: Completeness state for the exact account/window inputs. COMPLETE, BOUNDARY_INCOMPLETE and AMOUNT_UNKNOWN cannot be collapsed into a binary risk score.

evidence_ids.description: Semicolon-delimited exact Evidence keys. Every key must resolve, support the row proposition and retain its claim class and scope limitation.

control_id.description: Unique reconciliation-control key. Controls can test different grains; counts and monetary comparisons are never combined into one unexplained balance.

measure.description: Precisely named control measure including known versus complete scope. A passing count measure cannot substitute for unknown monetary completeness.

expected_value.description: Independent expected numerical control value when known. Null records a proposition whose true value is unavailable rather than a failed zero comparison.

actual_value.description: Reproduced value from the supplied rows. Null remains null when the corresponding measure is unavailable; never enter an attractive expected value by copying.

unit.description: Physical or analytical unit of the control, such as USD, rows, legs or account windows. The label determines what can validly be added or divided.

result.description: Control result or acceptance state. PASS applies to an executed synthetic check; it is not regulatory assurance or an operational approval.

calculation.description: Explicit arithmetic or set-membership expression supporting the control. It retains unknown components instead of replacing them with a rounded display.

report_narrative: Two accounts match the illustrative rapid-movement rule. One has a supported invoice explanation; the other needs further review. A separate account remains not assessable because an amount is unreadable.

The ten raw rows reconcile to eight processed transactions after the documented duplicate and exclusion decisions. The fictional scenario uses explicit amount, ratio and timing criteria; unreadable amounts remain outside assessable sums.
TM-F01: Account A received $10,000.00 and sent $9,500.00 within two hours of the first receipt; the 95.0% ratio meets TM-01. Purpose remains unsupported.
TM-F02: The 96.0% rule match is retained; a matched supplier invoice supports the $4,800.00 payment.
TM-F03: One unreadable amount prevents account-level completeness; $1,000.00 is only the known posted debit.

Known gross movement is $36,300.00 within the captured records. Account totals retain the relationship between incoming and outgoing activity; gross movement is not net loss, customer income or suspicious value.

RawTransactions retains all ten rows; CanonicalLedger contains the eight readable unique posted legs. Eligibility retains ten separate reasons. Credit-anchored diagnostics contain seven memberships over five distinct legs; their known membership gross of $42,800.00 is overlapping and is not unique movement. All three diagnostic windows extend beyond the supplied observation boundary and cannot be represented as complete rolling-window assessments.

Two accounts meet the raw illustrative rapid-movement criterion. One has a supported invoice explanation, while the other remains a review lead. An additional account is not assessable because an amount is unreadable; it cannot be scored as a negative.

Daily TM-01 and diagnostic rolling windows are separate measures. ReviewLedger retains four account review records with no human disposition recorded; the supported B invoice does not remove SR-002. ControlTotals preserves the failed monetary-completeness proposition even though row reconciliation passes.

The synthetic source rows and criterion definitions in file 10 support the arithmetic and matches. The public typology references do not supply a regulatory threshold or evidence of wrongdoing for these fictional accounts.
Review the unexplained match, preserve the invoice explanation without deleting the raw match, and repair the unreadable amount before rerunning the affected account.
